assertion: The net migration loss was slightly larger than the year before, though the income loss shrank from $4.18 billion.
New Hampshire gained a net 7,818 residents from Massachusetts, while Florida picked up 6,032. Together, those two states accounted for roughly 44% of Massachusetts' net migration loss.
Massachusetts lost a net $1.29 billion in adjusted gross income to Florida and $869 million to New Hampshire, together about 59% of the state's total.
Tax filers ages 26 to 34 made up 43% of the state's net loss of filers in 2024, and those earning $200,000 or more accounted for $2.32 billion, or 64%, of the net income loss.
independent_value: Matches Boston.com's relay of Pioneer; arithmetic 2.32/3.64 = 63.7%. Pioneer's own report not located.

assertion: New York sent the most newcomers to Massachusetts (13,394), followed by Florida (11,728) and California (8,728). ... net gain of 855 residents from New Jersey, plus smaller gains from Louisiana and Indiana.

The Massachusetts Department of Revenue preliminarily certified $3.38 billion in surtax collections for fiscal 2026, a record, and well above the $2.4 billion the state budget had assumed.
